clues.title: Google car: Follow car
text: A light green Toyota or dark green Mazda was escorting the Google car through most of Tunisia coverage, and if you look behind, you can almost always see them. Sometimes you won’t see it, so don’t rule out Tunisia if you can't spot the escort car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Tunisia usually has white road lines.
Outer road lines can be dashed or solid.
A few roads in Sfax have yellow middle lines.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Light Green Toyota
text: This light green Toyota follow car can be found everywhere in the northernmost part of Tunisia.
You will never see it south of Hammamet.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Dark Green Mazda
text: The dark green Mazda is the most common follow car in Tunisia.
This becomes apparent if you look at the coverage map, it can be found all the way from Hammamet to Djerba.
Aside from the darker colour, it can also be recognized by its military licence plate with a red strip on the left.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Tunis Follow Cars
text: Tunis, the capital of Tunisia, has a lot of different follow cars.
Most of them can be found all over the city.
The light green Toyota can also be spotted here.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Kairouan Follow Car
text: The city of Kairouan in central-northern Tunisia has this unique follow car, a white Mitsubishi.
The dark green follow car can also sometimes be spotted following the Mitsubishi.
**NOTE:**
Some white follow cars in Tunisia can look similar to the Kairouan car. However, none of them are Mitshubishis.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Djerba Follow Car
text: The island of Djerba is the only region of Tunisia where you are usually not accompanied by a follow car.
Most coverage completely lacks one.
While it is rare, this white Mercedes and the dark green follow car can be present.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Hilly Terrain
text: The area north of Tunis has a Mediterranean climate with hilly terrain.
The region is very agricultural and at the time the coverage was captured, almost all fields laid fallow.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Vegetated Hills
text: The area between Tunis and Hammamet looks similar to the area north of Tunis, but the hills tend to be higher and more vegetated.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Flat & Arid Landscape
text: The large middle region between Hammamet and Gabes is very flat, and more arid.
Olive tree plantations are common and the more south you go, the drier the landscape becomes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Desert Landscape
text: South of Gabes is where the landscape changes into something more akin to a desert.
A lot more rubbish and small white rocks can be found along the roads.
Olive tree plantations are still somewhat common.
A mountain range far in the distance is often visible to the southwest.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Djerba Vibe
text: The island of Djerba can sometimes have a distinct vibe.
There tend to be a lot of palm trees. Whitewashed, traditional buildings with blue doors and windows are common.
**NOTE:**
Not all locations on the island will have this distinct vibe.
A lack of a follow car is another good way to confirm that you are on Djerba

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Black Car
text: The Google car in Tunisia is black with a medium-length, thin antenna.
The colour of the car is not always perceptible.
Make sure to look around for other more helpful clues.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Follow Cars
text: One of the best ways to recognize Tunisia is that, in ~98% of coverage, the Google car is escorted by a follow car.
There are several different follow cars and these are four of the most commonly found ones.
Follow cars can be in front of the street view car, or very far behind.
Make sure to pan and zoom if you do not find them immediately.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Curbs
text: Red and white striped curbs are common in Tunisia.
Similar curbs are also common in Israel and Palestine.
Make sure to look for additional information!

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Stop sign: Stop Sign
text: Tunisia has a fairly unique stop sign with Arabic and Latin script.
Similar stop signs can be found in Jordan and the UAE.
However, Israel and Palestine use a different unique stop sign with a hand instead of text.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Direction sign: Direction Signs
text: Most direction signs have a white background with towns listed in Arabic and Latin script.
The font of the Latin script is usually quite distinctive.
Many direction signs include the capital Tunis, but this does not necessarily mean you are anywhere near that city.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Lake Bizerte
text: Bizerte Lake is instantly recognizable due to its teal coloured waters. There are slight hills to its south, with the rest of the area around the lake being flat. The city of Bizerte is located on the northeast side of the lake.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Traditional Blue Paint
text: Doors, windows, gates and other architectural elements are sometimes painted with this specific traditional shade of blue.
This shade of blue can be found all over the country, but is especially common on the island of Djerba, where buildings tend to be older and more traditional.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Gabes
text: If you see a large amount of palm trees in a single place, you are probably in Gabes.
NOTE: While Djerba also has many palm trees, the towns and surrounding area tend to look more rural.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: P1 sandy hills
text: On the P1 road northwest of Medinine, you can occasionally find sandy hills that look like this. These hills are quite unique, as most coverage in southern Tunisia is in very flat areas.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Sahli offroad
text: An offroad from road P12 southwest of Sousse can be recognised by the dark pavement surrounded by bright sandy soil combined with the east-west road angle. The eastern part of the road is fairly vegetated, with large numbers of prickly pears, while the western part of the road is very arid with little to no vegetation.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Caseway
text: You can easily recognise the Djerba-Zarzis causeway thanks to the water on both sides and the pipeline that is always present to your west.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Trekkers
text: Trekkers can be found all over the country, even in places far away from the area with car coverage. Coverage includes archaeological sites, forts, mosques, and a Star Wars set, among other things.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: Tunisia
text: Tunisian licence plates are black with white text.
NOTE: Military plates feature a small Tunisian flag on the left side of the plate, which is visible on the dark green follow car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
